Disease Outbreak Disrupts Cyprus Construction Materials Sector

An outbreak of viral gastroenteritis has struck the construction materials industry in Cyprus, causing significant operational disruptions as companies, including Vassiliko Cement Works Ltd, report high absenteeism among workers and temporary shutdowns of several production sites.

The outbreak, which began to be reported at the start of last week, has led to over 120 confirmed cases among site staff across the island, according to the Cyprus Association of Construction Materials Producers (CACMP). At Vassiliko Cement Works Ltd’s main plant, more than 15% of the workforce is currently on sick leave, prompting a reduction in production rates and a delay in scheduled shipments.

“Production capacity at our site has dropped by approximately 20% since the onset of the outbreak,” said Andreas Christou, site manager at Vassiliko Cement Works Ltd. “We are implementing enhanced hygiene protocols and working closely with local health authorities to contain the spread, but the situation remains challenging.”

Other companies, such as Limni Aggregates, have also scaled back shifts as a precaution. Industry analysts estimate that project delays and supply shortfalls could extend into the coming weeks if the outbreak is not swiftly brought under control. “The timing is especially difficult, as demand has been robust this quarter,” noted Eleni Papadopoulou, an industry analyst with Cyprus Construction Insights.

The CACMP has urged members to reinforce sanitation measures, adjust shift patterns, and provide additional personal protective equipment. “Our priority is the health and safety of our workforce,” stated CACMP President Giorgos Ioannou. “We are monitoring the situation closely and coordinating with public health officials.”

At press time, the outbreak was ongoing, with further updates expected as the situation develops.
